title: Flat affine scalar-extension comparison for global Hom
statement: Let $X,Y,Y\prime$ be schemes [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], with $X$ quasi-compact quasi-separated and $Y,Y\prime$ affine. Let $f:X\to Y$ be flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] and $g:Y\prime\to Y$. Set $X\prime=X\times_Y Y\prime$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. For perfect $M$ [def-pc-perfect-complex] and $N\in D_{QCoh}(X)$ [def-pc-derived-category], the canonical scalar-extension transpose $L(-\otimes_{\Gamma(Y)}\Gamma(Y\prime))RHom_X(M,N)\to RHom_{X\prime}(Lg_X^*M,Lg_X^*N)$ [def-pc-global-derived-rhom, def-pc-global-hom-pullback-comparison] is invertible. The transpose uses the evaluation-mate pullback comparison, normalized Leray isomorphism, and scalar-square identification. The module and sheaf localization universes may be chosen independently.

proof.text: Flatness gives stalkwise Tor independence. Express internal Hom as the perfect dual tensored with N. Apply torIndependent_perfect_tensor_baseChange to this tensor, then reuse the proved baseChangeMap_naturality helper from AffineMorphismHomOutOfPerfect and use isomorphism cancellation to transport invertibility to internal Hom.

The perfect evaluation-mate pullback map theta is invertible. Internal Hom and its direct image are quasi-coherent. Apply the mixed affine sections mate identity to the pullback/direct-image adjunct of theta. Cancel that adjunction equivalence and identify the scalar transpose definitionally with mixedAffineGlobalHomBaseChangeMap. Its factorization consists of isomorphisms and functor images of the sheaf base-change map and theta, hence is invertible. The definitions of theta and the scalar transpose use the mixed tensor comparison, normalized mixed Leray comparison, and mixed scalar extension adjunction; these original dependencies remain required.

proof_origin.note: Reduction via sheaf tensor base change, naturality and isomorphism cancellation, followed by the general mixed affine sections mate. Preserves the original statement and independent localization universes.
